title: Understanding General Living Expenses Salary Packaging and Your Hourly to Annual Pay
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay with our guide. Includes tax, super, and general living expenses salary packaging explained for Australian workers.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

To estimate your annual gross pay, multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full‑time employee, the standard week is 38 hours. So the formula is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 hours per week × 52 weeks**

If you work part‑time or different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for budgeting and comparing job offers.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38‑hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. Many jobs are covered by industry or occupation awards that set higher minimum rates. Always check your award or agreement for the correct base rate.

If you are looking at average pay, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full‑time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. This is an average across all industries and states, not the median for your specific job. For all employees including part‑time, total average weekly earnings were $1,579.20.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of their base hourly rate. On [the timesheet](/), you can enter your base rate and check a box to add the casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading; the tool applies it automatically.

Superannuation (super) is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer pays an extra $7,200 into your super fund. This estimate shows super as an additional amount, not deducted from your pay.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: 45% on the excess over $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. This estimate uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here. It does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or salary packaging.

### Understanding General Living Expenses Salary Packaging

Some employers, especially in the not‑for‑profit sector, offer **general living expenses salary packaging**. This allows you to use pre‑tax income to pay for everyday costs such as rent, groceries, utilities, or mortgage payments. By reducing your taxable income, salary packaging can lower the amount of tax and Medicare levy you pay. However, this estimate does not include any salary packaging arrangements. If your employer offers this benefit, you should factor it into your own calculations. For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Using the Timesheet and Other Resources

The timesheet on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate, add casual loading, and see your estimated annual gross, fortnightly pay, super, and tax. Remember that the fortnightly amount is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For example, if your weekly gross is $1,000, your fortnightly gross is $2,000.

You can also explore our [pay guides](/blog) for award‑specific information, [reference tables](/data) for tax and super rates, and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for industry benchmarks. If you want to check the current minimum wage, visit our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. For a deeper look at how your take‑home pay is calculated, see [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home).

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is your hourly rate multiplied by hours per week times 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
